source.title: Tracing distinguishability through transformer processing with stochastic LayerNorm

page_placements.theme: Identifying induction heads: scores miss heads or diverge from causal role

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports measurements related to induction-head motifs, but does not directly test any listed version: it does not test the induction circuit, training-time formation, in-context learning, or universality across models.
record.gate_note: The paper measures how much single-token perturbation distinguishability is retained by attention-head projections and reports prefix-matching scores for some heads. These are related findings, not tests of the listed claims. Results about rate budgets and distillation performance do not measure induction-head formation or in-context learning. Induction-head findings cited from other work are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study validates its own method, Bhattacharyya distinguishability through stochastic LayerNorm reads, against known induction heads in GPT-2 small. It uses prefix-matching scores and prior induction-head lists (Nanda mosaic, Wang et al.) as reference labels, and reports how well its K-selectivity measure lines up with them. It does not test the induction circuit, the phase change, in-context learning, universality, data dependence or formation stages. So this is better described as using the finding as a tool (T4) than as discussion only (T6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present stochastic-read distinguishability as a functional complement to point-representation geometry. They report that heads with K-selective sensitivity largely coincide with heads previously linked to induction, including some with weak or absent prefix-matching scores. They call the work a proof of concept.
record.recipe_differences: Uses stochastic LayerNorm reads and perturbation-distinguishability measurements in a fine-tuned GPT-2 model; it does not reproduce the induction-head identification or training-time measurements in the original sources.

fits_no_version.finding: Seven middle-layer GPT-2 heads retain K-projection distinguishability above a random-projection baseline (about 0.1). L5H8 and L4H7 keep strong K selectivity despite near-zero prefix-matching scores.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Key-projection sensitivity to token distinctions can flag induction-adjacent heads that prefix-matching attention scores miss.

record.problems: For the induction-adjacent results, the text gives no exact key-selectivity fractions or prefix-matching scores; the plotted values are not stated numerically. The results are from GPT-2-small at one rate budget and do not assess other models or training runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported separately in the text. Exact per-head fractions and plotted prefix-matching values in Figure 5 were not extracted because they are figure-only.

untested.parts: Previous-token-head composition and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism are not examined.
No tracking over training; the model is distillation-fine-tuned from pretrained GPT-2.
No measurement of in-context learning or of induction heads' share of it.
Only one model (GPT-2 small), and the presence of induction heads there is taken from prior work rather than newly tested across families or runs.
Data and training-setup effects on induction formation are not studied.

record.verdict_notes: The induction-head correspondence rests on cited sources (Nanda 2022 mosaic; Wang et al. 2023), not on this study's own induction tests. The model is a stochastic, distillation-fine-tuned GPT-2 small, not the original deterministic model. No verdicts are given because no version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test previous-token-head composition or the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
Does not track induction heads, in-context learning, or training loss over training time.
Does not measure in-context learning or whether induction heads carry most of it.
Does not test induction behaviour across model families, sizes, or training runs, or in other architectures or modalities.
Does not test how data or training setup affects induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not compare few-shot task learning with induction-head or other mechanisms.
Does not measure the stages or timing of induction-head formation.

rows.subject: GPT-2 stochastic model
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of upstream Bhattacharyya distance retained by attention-head key projections for minimally perturbed text pairs.

conditions.value: 80 minimally perturbed pairs; noun replacements; retained swaps with at most 50 nats of Bhattacharyya distance at the layer 5 attention read immediately following the perturbation
seven middle-layer heads reported in aggregate

rows.measure: Fraction of upstream Bhattacharyya distance retained by K projections
rows.baseline: Random 64-dimensional projections preserve around 0.1; the shaded band is the 5–95% spread.
rows.value: Seven middle-layer heads stand out above the random-projection baseline; exact fractions are figure-only.
rows.note: The paper reports the seven-head result as an aggregate. It says six of the seven heads have an independently reported connection to induction, citing prior work; those cited results are not this study's results. This measurement is key-projection selectivity, not the induction mechanism itself.
rows.check: This row is the study's own method output: K-projection distinguishability against a random-projection baseline. It does not measure induction behaviour, so the state relative to any version cannot be determined. The induction link for six of the seven heads comes from cited work, not this study. Exact values are figure-only.

relation.reason: The study compares K-projection distinguishability with prior induction-head identifications and prefix-matching scores to assess its own method.

tranche.reason: Known induction-head characterizations serve as references for evaluating the study's distinguishability method; its results do not test a listed claim version.
